extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and U.S. patent examiners (U.S. patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for filing, entering, publishing, disapproving, and responding to preliminary amendments and for treating replies to non-final Office actions during U.S. patent prosecution (MPEP §§714.01–714.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification required when preliminary amendment modifies specification (other than benefit claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice requires filing a substitute specification because a preliminary amendment adds or amends the specification (other than only adding/amending a benefit claim), the applicant must file the substitute specification or explain why it is not necessary to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary amendment only amends a benefit claim, applicant may reply explaining a substitute specification should not have been required. If the preliminary amendment contains other amendments to the specification (other than the claims), a substitute specification will be required; a reply without the substitute specification will be treated as incomplete with no new time period for reply. Requiring a substitute specification ensures compliance with redacted-publication limitations (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(v)) and allows the Office to publish any new matter included on the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments to claims/abstract may be published without substitute specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment to the claims or abstract in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(c) or 1.121(b)(2) that includes a complete claim listing or replacement abstract can be published as submitted without a substitute specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no need to file a preliminary amendment to the claims on filing; making the new claim set part of the originally filed specification may avoid application size fees because both the specification (including claims) and any preliminary amendment are used in counting pages per 37 CFR 1.16(s). Claims submitted on filing should be the set intended for examination and, if part of the specification on sequentially numbered pages (37 CFR 1.52(b)(5)), need no status identifiers or change markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment filed at national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 is not original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment filed with a submission to enter the national stage of a PCT application under 35 U.S.C. 371 is not part of the original disclosure under 37 CFR 1.115(a) because it was not present on the international filing date accorded under PCT Article 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, a 'Notice to File Corrected Application Papers' requiring a substitute specification will not ordinarily be mailed in an international application even if the national stage submission includes a preliminary amendment. See MPEP §1893.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after RCE are not preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Because a request for continued examination (RCE) is not a new application, an amendment filed before the first Office action after the filing of the RCE is not a preliminary amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §706.07(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Any preliminary amendment, regardless of when filed, must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., include a complete listing of all claims and each section of the amendment must begin on a separate sheet of paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments in a transmittal letter will not comply. If a preliminary amendment filed after the filing date fails to comply, applicant will get a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment and a non-extendable one-month period to correct; if no corrective action, examination will commence without considering the proposed changes. If a preliminary amendment present on the filing date fails to comply, OIPE will notify applicant and give two months to correct to avoid abandonment. See MPEP §714.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid filing preliminary amendments when possible (publication/timing concern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a preliminary amendment is not recommended because changes made by it may not be reflected in the patent application publication if technical preparations for publication have begun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical preparations generally begin four months before publication. Applicants may avoid preliminary amendments by incorporating desired amendments into the specification text (including a new claim set) when filing, even in continuations/divisionals; a clean copy reflecting parent amendments and a copy of the prior oath/declaration may be submitted so long as no new matter is included. See 37 CFR 1.63(d)(1)(iii) and MPEP §201.06(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment present on filing date may be part of original disclosure (post- and pre-9/21/2004 rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept 21, 2004, a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure. For applications filed before that date, it is part of the original disclosure only if referred to in the first executed oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If present on filing date but the oath/declaration does not refer to it, Office generally will not screen it for new matter; it is applicant's obligation to ensure it contains no new matter. If it does contain new matter, applicant must provide a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 referring to the preliminary amendment. Failure to submit the supplemental oath removes safeguards implied by the oath's inventor review and duty to disclose (37 CFR 1.56). An examiner discovering unsupported subject matter may require (1) an oath/declaration referring to the amendment, (2) an amendment cancelling unsupported subject matter, or (3) a request for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments must be timely (timing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary amendments should accompany the application or be filed after the application has its application number and filing date so the amendments include appropriate identifications; amendments filed after the mail date of the first Office action are not preliminary amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the date of receipt of the amendment is later than the mail date of the first Office action and is not responsive to that action, the Office will not mail a new Office action but will advise applicant the amendment is nonresponsive and that a timely responsive reply is necessary to avoid abandonment. See MPEP §502 and §714.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may disapprove preliminary amendment (statutory bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 will be entered unless disapproved by the Director under 37 CFR 1.115(b). Disapproval grounds include cancellation of all claims without presenting new/substitute claims and undue interference with preparation of a first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disapproval for undue interference considers (i) the state of preparation of the first Office action as of receipt date and (ii) the nature of any changes that would result from entry. A preliminary amendment will not be disapproved under the undue-interference ground if filed no later than the listed time periods (e.g., three months from filing date under 1.53(b), filing date of a CPA under 1.53(d), or three months from entry of national stage under 1.491). Those time periods are not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment cancelling all claims without replacements will be disapproved
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a preliminary amendment seeking cancellation of all claims in the application without presenting any new or substitute claims, the Office will not enter such an amendment and will treat the application as containing only a single claim for fee calculation purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an amendment typically fails 37 CFR 1.121(c) requiring a complete claim listing. The Office will send a notice of non-compliant amendment and require an amendment in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121. See Exxon Corp. v. Phillips Petroleum Co. and MPEP §601.01(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Undue interference denial: two-condition test
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry of a preliminary amendment may be denied as unduly interfering only when (A) the examiner has devoted a significant amount of time preparing a first Office action before receipt of the amendment, and (B) entry of the amendment would require significant additional time in preparing the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both conditions are met, the examiner must obtain SPE approval before denying entry. Factors satisfying the first condition include substantial time spent on prior art search or drafting. Examples of changes that may satisfy the second condition: amending claims, adding numerous new claims, changing scope of claims via spec amendments, raising new matter issues, including arguments, submitting affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131/1.132, or including evidence traversing rejections from a parent application. This list is not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: When denying entry for undue interference is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Denying entry under 37 CFR 1.115(b)(2) is inappropriate if either the examiner has NOT devoted a significant amount of time on the Office action before receipt, or entry of the amendment would NOT require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the examiner spent significant time, entry should not be disapproved if the amendment merely cancels some pending claims, amends claims to overcome rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph, amends claims to place the application in condition for allowance, or only includes changes previously suggested by the examiner that would not require significant additional time. See MPEP §714.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.46 when denying entry due to undue interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.46 should be used to notify applicant that entry of a preliminary amendment is denied because it would unduly interfere with preparation of the Office action (37 CFR 1.115(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph includes placeholders for receipt date, state of preparation completed by the examiner as of receipt date, and brief explanation of how entry would require significant additional time. Examiner notes instruct use of receipt date under 37 CFR 1.6, examples of state of preparation, and examples of how entry would require more time (e.g., conduct additional prior art search or extensive revisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to non-final Office actions must be fully responsive (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the applicant or patent owner must file a written reply that distinctly and specifically points out supposed errors and replies to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments showing specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that claims define a patentable invention without specific explanation does not comply. If replying with amendments, the applicant must clearly point out the patentable novelty and show how amendments avoid the references or objections. See 37 CFR 1.111(b)–(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on supplemental replies
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply that is supplemental to a §1.111(b)-compliant reply will not be entered as a matter of right except as provided in §1.111(a)(2)(ii); the Office may enter a supplemental reply only if it is clearly limited to specific categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted supplemental-reply topics include cancellation of claims, adoption of examiner suggestions, placement in condition for allowance, reply to a requirement made after the first reply, correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors), or simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply filed during a period when Office action is suspended under §1.103(a) or (c) will be entered. See 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reply: formal compliance or specific traversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reply to a requirement is necessary for further consideration of claims or allowable subject matter has been indicated, a complete reply must either comply with formal requirements or specifically traverse each formal requirement not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawing and specification corrections, presentation of a new oath, etc., are generally formal matters; however, when merits require, such formal corrections may be insisted upon prior to indication of allowable subject matter. The line between formal and merit matters is not sharp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not fully responsive may be treated variably by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is not fully responsive to a non-final Office action, the examiner may (A) accept it as an adequate reply to avoid abandonment, (B) notify applicant that the reply must be completed within the remaining time for reply to avoid abandonment, or (C) set a new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) for applicant to complete the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment depends on whether the amendment is bona fide, whether sufficient time remains to file within the original reply period, and the nature of the deficiency. If amendment substantially responds but omits a minor matter, examiner may act on the amendment and issue a new Office action reiterating unaddressed items. For serious deficiencies, examiner should require correction within remaining time or set a one-month period if insufficient remaining time. Examiner should not further examine merits until omissions are timely supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and limits for granting new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may be given a new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to supply an inadvertent omission where the reply is bona fide and substantially complete; this is discretionary and depends on bona fides, available time, and nature of the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.135(c) applies only to inadvertent omissions, not deliberate omissions. Examples of non-bona fide omissions: deliberate refusal to make an election of species, or cancelling all claims without presenting new claims. If a new time period is set, applicant must supply the omission within that period (or extensions under 1.136(a)) to avoid abandonment; applicant may alternatively file a continuing application during this period. The practice does not apply after final Office action; amendments after final are entered only if they place the application in condition for allowance or better form for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final treatment and examiner discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final Office action, the examiner cannot give time under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to supply an omission; amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or better form for appeal, otherwise they are not approved for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply to a final substantially places the application in condition for allowance, an examiner may request applicant authorize an examiner's amendment to correct the omission and then the date of reply is the date of authorization. Examiner may also enter the reply, withdraw finality, and issue a new Office action (non-final, final, or closing prosecution on merits) at examiner discretion. Applicant responsibility remains to take necessary action to provide a complete reply under 37 CFR 1.113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.95 for bona fide but non-fully responsive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.95 (and optionally 7.95.01) should be used where a bona fide reply to a non-final Office action is not fully responsive; it notifies applicant of omissions and gives a one-month (30-day) time period to supply omissions to avoid abandonment (extensions possible under 1.136(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This practice does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission or where the application is subject to a final Office action. Paragraph 7.95.01 specifically requests that applicant submit argument under the heading 'Remarks' explaining disagreements and discussing the references applied against the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(b),(c),(d),(h) required for responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment which does not comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.121(b), (c), (d), and (h) may be held not fully responsive to an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of 1.121 include formatting, complete claim listings, and other procedural formalities; failure to comply can result in treatment under MPEP §714 (non-responsive/amendment not entered).
